summary.title: SecureNova AI Identity Security
summary.description: Proposed logical architecture for an AI-powered application using Auth0, AI agents, an external LLM, RAG, MCP and protected internal APIs.

data.name: Customer / Human User
data.description: External customer initiating authentication and chat requests.

data.name: Auth0 Identity Provider
data.description: OIDC identity provider that authenticates users and issues access tokens.

data.name: AI Application / Orchestrator
data.description: Validates incoming requests and coordinates AI agent execution.

data.name: AI Agent
data.description: Executes model and tool workflows using a scoped service identity.

threats.title: AI Agent Identity Spoofing
threats.description: An attacker may steal or forge AI agent credentials and impersonate the legitimate AI agent. This could allow unauthorized access to the MCP Server and execution of tools using the agent's identity.
threats.mitigation: Validate signed authentication tokens, verify issuer and audience claims, use short-lived agent credentials, enforce agent identity verification at the MCP Server, and apply least-privilege permissions.

data.name: External LLM Provider
data.description: Third-party model inference service outside SecureNova's trust domain.

data.name: RAG Retrieval Service
data.description: Retrieves approved knowledge chunks for model context.

data.name: Vector Database
data.description: Stores embeddings and indexed knowledge chunks.

data.name: MCP Server
data.description: Exposes controlled tools to the AI agent.

data.name: Internal Business API
data.description: Enforces authorization for internal business operations.

data.name: Secrets Vault
data.description: Stores application, agent and provider credentials.

data.name: Security Monitoring / SIEM
data.description: Collects authentication, agent and tool audit events.

threats.title: Tool Invocation Parameter Tampering
threats.description: An attacker may modify the parameters of a tool invocation between the AI Agent and MCP Server. For example, an attacker may change the customer ID in an account-balance request to access another customer's information or trigger an unintended operation.
threats.mitigation: Validate all tool invocation parameters, enforce server-side authorization, reject unexpected input, and verify the integrity of sensitive requests.

threats.title: MCP Server Denial of Service
threats.description: An attacker may send an excessive number of tool invocation requests to the MCP Server, consuming system resources and preventing legitimate AI agent requests from being processed.
threats.mitigation: Implement rate limiting, request quotas, request timeouts, resource monitoring and traffic filtering to maintain service availability.

threats.title: Sensitive Customer Information Disclosure
threats.description: The MCP Server may expose sensitive customer information to the AI Agent through tool responses. Excessive data returned by the tool may result in unauthorized disclosure of personal or financial information.
threats.mitigation: Apply least-privilege access, return only the information required by the requested operation, enforce authorization checks, and encrypt sensitive information during transmission.
